Requirement Statement: The application shall execute the five reference vectors in a fixed, documented order on every test run.
Inference Rationale: Executing each vector exactly once does not by itself define a repeatable sequence. A fixed order is required for the startup result and serial log to be deterministic and for the five reported results to be unambiguously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Repeated resets with the same firmware produce the five vector executions and result lines in the same documented order.
Parameters / Constraints: Fixed execution order shall be documented and shall remain consistent across runs.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: All five vectors have been executed once in the defined order.
Failure Behavior: A deviation from the defined order shall produce a FAIL result and shall not be reported as PASS.
Comments / Open Questions: The PRD lists the vectors in an apparent order but does not explicitly state whether that order is normative.

Requirement Statement: The application shall complete clock and FPU initialization before starting ML runtime initialization or executing FP32 inference.
Source Text / Evidence:
On reset, initialize the MCU clock, FPU and serial console.
Initialize the generated ML network and all required activation, context and I/O buffers.
Inference Rationale: The ML runtime and FP32 inference depend on a valid processor clock and usable FPU. Without an enforced initialization dependency, inference may execute with incorrect clock or floating-point configuration and the required results cannot be trusted.
Acceptance Criteria: Instrumentation or review demonstrates that clock and FPU initialization complete before ML runtime initialization and before the first inference call.
Parameters / Constraints: Initialization dependency order: MCU clock and FPU before ML runtime initialization and inference.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: The processor environment required for ML initialization and FP32 inference is configured before those operations begin.
Failure Behavior: If the required initialization order cannot be achieved, the test shall fail and shall not execute inference.

Requirement Statement: The application shall detect an unsuccessful console transmission for each required startup, vector-result and final-status message.
Source Text / Evidence: Any initialization failure, inference failure, non-finite output, deinitialization failure or console transmission failure shall cause the test to fail.
Inference Rationale: Treating console transmission failure as a test failure is not verifiable unless the firmware observes the transmission result or timeout for each required message. Without detection, lost output could be incorrectly treated as a successful test.
Acceptance Criteria: A forced or simulated unsuccessful console transmission causes the test status to become FAIL and prevents a PASS summary.
Parameters / Constraints: Every required console transmission shall have an observable success or failure result.
Preconditions: The serial console has been initialized.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Each required message is either confirmed transmitted or causes the test to enter the failure path.
Failure Behavior: An unsuccessful transmission shall set the test result to FAIL; the application shall report the condition if further console output remains available.
Comments / Open Questions: The PRD does not specify a transmission timeout or UART error-detection mechanism.

Requirement Statement: Each ML_VECTOR result line shall identify the reference vector and indicate the outcome of its FP32 comparison.

Acceptance Criteria: The captured log contains exactly one ML_VECTOR line for each of positive, first_clamped, second_clamped, zero_input and both_clamped, and each line contains an objectively interpretable comparison outcome.
Parameters / Constraints: One uniquely attributable result line per named vector.
Preconditions: A reference vector has been executed and compared.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: The vector's comparison result is observable in the serial log.
Failure Behavior: A missing, duplicate or unidentifiable vector result shall cause the overall test to fail.
Comments / Open Questions: The PRD does not define the complete ML_VECTOR line grammar or the exact pass/fail token.

Requirement Statement: The complete startup and five-vector test sequence shall execute without runtime stack overflow and with all stack, static, activation, context and I/O storage within the target SRAM allocation.
Source Text / Evidence:
The generated linker memory placement shall fit within the target MCU Flash and SRAM limits.
The application shall not require dynamic heap allocation for the test sequence.
Inference Rationale: A link-time fit does not prove that runtime stack use remains within SRAM during initialization and inference. Stack exhaustion or collision with model buffers can corrupt outputs and prevent the required deterministic PASS/FAIL result.
Acceptance Criteria: Worst-case execution of startup and all five vectors completes without stack overflow, memory corruption or overlap, and the map/runtime evidence shows all required storage remains within the 256 KiB SRAM allocation.
Parameters / Constraints: All runtime storage, including stack and ML activation, context and I/O buffers, shall fit within the target SRAM allocation.
Preconditions: The final linked firmware and its memory map are available.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: The complete test sequence executes without runtime memory exhaustion or corruption.
Failure Behavior: A memory-bound violation shall reject the firmware and shall not be reported as a valid PASS result.
Resource Impact: Runtime stack and ML buffers consume the 256 KiB SRAM budget.
Comments / Open Questions: The PRD does not provide a stack-size or runtime high-water-mark limit.
